prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: square seamless albedo-only source tile for a low-poly fantasy forest terrain material
Primary request: Create a reusable forest-floor moss ground albedo for shaded old-growth woodland clearings and humid jungle pockets.
Style/medium: muted painterly low-poly fantasy ground in the understated Eloria material style; broad readable color masses and modest surface detail.
Composition/framing: flat orthographic square texture; evenly distributed soft ground variation; left-right and top-bottom edges must meet seamlessly when tiled, with no frame or focal patch.
Color palette: deep moss green, olive, dark umber soil and a few subdued leaf-brown notes; keep saturation restrained.
Materials/textures: soft mottled woodland loam with irregular low-contrast moss patches, faint decomposed leaf matter and sparse small rootlike fibers integrated into the ground; no distinct leaf or plant silhouettes; 4 metre intended terrain repeat.
Lighting/mood: uniform neutral diffuse albedo only, no shaded canopy or light pools.
Constraints: both-axis seamless tile; moderate detail that stays calm at gameplay distance; texture coloration only.
Avoid: standalone plants, leaves as recognizable objects, flowers, twigs, roots crossing the surface, bright lime green, dense high-frequency noise, large centerpiece, lighting gradients, directional shadows, highlights, perspective, horizon, borders, frame, text, logo, watermark.
